detection_signals.reasoning: The window shows 22 failed login attempts across 15 distinct IPs targeting 8 distinct usernames within a very short span of 1.52 seconds. This coordinated multi-IP activity targeting multiple accounts indicates a distributed credential stuffing or brute force attack.

assessment_at_capture.rationale: The evidence shows a strong, deliberate attack pattern consisting of 22 failed login attempts across 15 distinct IPs targeting 8 distinct usernames in a very short span of 1.52 seconds. Threat intelligence confirms that the top source IPs are associated with a known botnet and distributed credential-stuffing campaigns. Although all login attempts failed (0 successful logins), the malicious reputation and coordinated multi-IP nature warrant a High severity rating and immediate escalation.

correlation.intel_summary: All 5 checked source IPs (203.0.113.55, 203.0.113.35, 203.0.113.31, 203.0.113.24, 203.0.113.59) were flagged as malicious, categorized under botnet activity associated with distributed credential-stuffing campaigns.
correlation.enrichment_notes: The threat intelligence lookups confirm that all five top source IPs belong to a known distributed credential-stuffing botnet range (203.0.113.0/24). Combined with the high request rate (15.15 req/sec across 16 distinct IPs and 22 failed login attempts against 8 common usernames with 0 successful logins), this strongly points to a coordinated, automated credential-stuffing attack rather than isolated brute-forcing. The malicious intel makes the incident significantly more concerning, validating the automated nature of the traffic and confirming hostile intent.
